### Description

ACME renewal fails due to certmagic trying to find the certificate in the wrong directory. Initial issuance works just fine though. Certificates located in `/var/lib/gitea/https/certificates/ca.mydomain.com-acme-acme-directory/` but renewals check for the certificate in `/var/lib/gitea/.local/share/certmagic/certificates/acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory/`.

certmagic prints: `error while checking if stored certificate is also expiring soon`

Relevant parts of my config are below:

```
; ACME support

PROTOCOL = https
ENABLE_ACME = true
ACME_ACCEPTTOS = true
ACME_URL = https://ca.mydomain.com/acme/acme/directory
ACME_DIRECTORY = https
ACME_EMAIL = nan@nan
```

### Gitea Version

1.21.9

comment.body:
Got the same on Forgejo 7.x/Gitea 1.21.x. Converting to Gitea paths, I was able to bandaid until bugfix with something like:

```
	sudo cp -r /var/lib/gitea/https/certificates /var/lib/gitea/.local/share/certmagic/certificates
	sudo systemctl stop gitea
	sudo systemctl start gitea
```

Both directories were updated during the certificate renewal.

Note: I'm not sure manually stopping and starting the SystemD daemon was necessary.

issue.title: Trigger based alert doesn't fire
issue.body:
I recently discovered alert2 and it's so much better than built-in alert.

I do have an issue with trigger based alerts.
1. Condition is mandatory - why is that? Maybe I am missing something? In automations it is optional...
2. Following alert doesn't fire regardless of  sensor.entry_door_battery state:
```
  - domain: entry_door
    name: battery_full
    trigger:
      - platform: numeric_state
        entity_id: sensor.entry_door_battery
        above: 79
    condition: "{{ true }}
```
I could put above 79 in condition, but I don't want alert fired each time sensor.entry_door_battery increments by 1.

comment.body:
I don't want to impose, but it would absolutely be better to natively support manual deactivation. Not only because it would be a cleaner use of the integration (no need for python hack), but also because implementation would spill over to trigger based alerts as well.

I'll give you an example:
### Alert if I forgot to charge my ebike after arriving home
This is implemented by having a one hour timer that starts when I arrive home. The automation cancels the timer if power consumption in smart socket rises to about 100W. But if the timer manages to finish, I use that as a trigger for an alert. Which is great and all, but that alert is not active after it fires, even though I didn't fix the problem. Ideally, it should stay active until I manage to get my butt down to the garage and attach the battery to the charger. Only then it would be appropriate to deactivate the alert.

What I am trying to say is, having a manual deactivation option makes sense for both, condition and trigger based alerts. It is useful when there are conditions and actions required to deactivate an alert that cannot be modeled in HA. Like a person checking cameras, or attaching a charger to a battery.

On another note, there is one small improvement I would propose: different icons for acknowledged and unacknowledged alerts. I am using auto entities card instead of your custom card in my main dashboard, and it's simply not possible to differentiate between the both types.

Finally I have to say I am really fortunate I discovered your integration. Seems to me HA has been neglecting this area for so long. A clear indication of this is the fact that you have to fully restart HA (not just YAML config) when making changes to builtin alert integration. But it's a really important area. I mean, it's of no use having all those fancy automations, but not realizing sensors dying, glitching, dropping out of network, batteries going empty, etc. I was especially impressed the way you designed generator patterns. Currently I have 30 alerts. I can't imagine configuring them one by one.

Happy holidays and wish you all the best

  need to be manually satisfied by the user, increasing their ease of use. - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `998 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/998>`_
- tox will inject the ``TOX_PARALLEL_ENV`` environment variable, set to the current running tox environment name,
  only when running in parallel mode. - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1139 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1139>`_
- Parallel children now save their output to a disk logfile  - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1143 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1143>`_
- Parallel children now are added to ``--result-json``  - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1159 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1159>`_
- Display pattern and ``sys.platform`` with platform mismatch - by :user:`blueyed`.
  `1176 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1176>`_
- Setting the environment variable ``TOX_REPORTER_TIMESTAMP`` to ``1`` will enable showing for each output line its delta
  since the tox startup. This can be especially handy when debugging parallel runs.- by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1203 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1203>`_


Documentation
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Add a ``poetry`` examples to packaging - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1163 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1163>`_

- Removed code that sometimes caused a difference in results between ``--parallel`` and ``-p`` when using ``posargs`` - by :user:`timdaman`
  `1192 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1192>`_


Features
^^^^^^^^

- tox now auto-provisions itself if needed (see :ref:`auto-provision`). Plugins or minimum version of tox no longer
  need to be manually satisfied by the user, increasing their ease of use. - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `998 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/998>`_

  `1143 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1143>`_

  `1159 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1159>`_

- Setting the environment variable ``TOX_REPORTER_TIMESTAMP`` to ``1`` will enable showing for each output line its delta

  `1203 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1203>`_

^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Add a ``poetry`` examples to packaging - by :user:`gaborbernat`
  `1163 <https://github.com/tox-dev/tox/issues/1163>`_
